correctness.rationale: Weighted K_{a,b} tree degree generating polynomial P X^(b-1)Y^(a-1) follows from the standard complete multipartite matrix-tree theorem. Supplying unit current between two a-side vertices gives R_eff=(1/x1+1/x2)/Y and edge-insertion determinant lemma gives Z1=P X^(b-1)Y^(a-2)(Y+x1+x2). Dividing and extracting degree-one coefficients yields pA=(1-1/a)^(b-1), endpoint pA*(b+1)/(b+2), and nonendpoint B-side pB'=(b+1)/(b+2)(1-1/b)^(a-2), so the displayed Δ follows by subtraction. For a>=3 the first term increases with b and second decreases; at b=a-1 sign is negative, at b=a positive; a=2,b=1 gives exact equality via 0^0=1. Checked source verifier parses real graph Laplacian cofactors and enumerates small trees, plus 120x120 exact signs; script inspected, not rerun. Full infinite proof algebraic.

This quantifies a nonmonotone edge perturbation on an elementary natural graph family and can inform random tree sensitivity; despite standard determinant-lemma tools the evaluated sign reversal is not a routine standalone textbook identity.

final_claim: For a>=2,b>=1, adding one within-a-part edge to K_{a,b} changes expected total leaf number by 2/(b+2)[(1-1/b)^(a-2)-(1-1/a)^(b-1)], positive iff b>=a, zero only (a,b)=(2,1), negative otherwise.
limitations: Uniform labeled spanning trees; one new edge within a fixed part; expected leaf count only, not distributional ordering or multiple additions.
